AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disease that affects young women in reproductive age. It has mainly three different clinical presentations: superficial (peritoneal), ovarian (endometriomas) and deep endometriosis (DE). The last one is the most advanced form of the disease, frequently impairing fertility and harming women's quality of life (QoL).

AbstractText.Label: EVIDENCE ACQUISITION
AbstractText.content: We conducted a systematic review on the surgical treatment of DE in the last ten years focusing on its benefits to improve QoL and for pain relief as well as related surgical complications.

AbstractText.Label: EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS
AbstractText.content: Twenty-three studies were included for qualitative analysis. Overall, included studies showed a relevant improvement in QoL as well as in pain scores using specific questionnaires and the ten-point Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) for pain.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Until further comparative studies regarding medical versus surgical treatment for DE are concluded, currently, surgery is the best option for patients with DE and severe pain (VAS>7).
